notes: Derived ABox edit for relation-property coverage (transitivity). Same derived structure as literature_arts-replace-0004 (painting, museum, city, country), but on located_in, so the continent query tests transitivity of 'located in', and the second indeterminate query compares two museums' countries (fol) instead of asking a premise again. Derivability likely: the country is almost never stated (1 exact hit) while both movable premises are stated thousands of times; country co-occurrence is not low (Vermeer was Dutch), so not very_likely. Worlds: the painting moves (w1) or the Mauritshuis moves (w2); 'The Hague is in the Netherlands' and the museum-to-country rule are firm, so worlds where they give way are dropped. w2 is the minority world (3,043 exact 'Mauritshuis in The Hague') and lists the side facts that go with it (the museum's other holdings move with it). Brazil is clearly false and crosses a continent, so the transitivity query discriminates; Japan was avoided because the painting was lent to Tokyo exhibitions, which could make the new value look like a confusion. R1: the painting has toured (e.g. to San Francisco in 2013), so prompts ask where it is located or held, not where it is on display. Near query (the Rijksmuseum's city) is not a premise; the Rijksmuseum's country is a bridge of the fol query only. Records that share the Mauritshuis premise must not be added alongside this one.
